if [ -z "${COST_COMPILER:-}" ]; then
    sh tools/census_compiler.sh "$compiler"
fi
[ -x "$compiler" ] || { echo "cost: no census compiler at $compiler"; exit 1; }

src=$out/src
mkdir -p "$src/build"
git archive "$snapshot" | tar -x -C "$src"
cp "$compiler" "$src/build/avra"
find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name 'avra_hot.bc' -o -name 'avra_hot.inc' \) \
    -exec cp {} "$src/build/" \;
printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" > "$out/snapshot"
cache=$root/$out/cache

# One run of the census compiler in the snapshot, once what it reads is older than the stamp window:
# its census to <name>.out, what it printed to <name>.stdout.
counted() {
    name=$1; shift
    sleep 3
    started=$(date +%s)
    # the census reports at exit only where the run accounts (AVRA_MEM_STATS)
    (cd "$src" && AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 \
        sh "$root/tools/memcap.sh" "${COST_CAP_MB:-8000}" taskset -c 0 build/avra "$@" \
        > "$root/$out/$name.stdout" 2> "$root/$out/$name.out") || {
        tail -20 "$out/$name.out"; echo "cost: $name failed ($*)"; exit 1; }
    echo "cost: $name $(($(date +%s) - started)) s"
}

# One warm findings run of the cli, its `worked:` line kept as <name>.out, its census beside it.
warm() {
    counted "$1" tapes --findings packages/cli
    mv "$out/$1.out" "$out/$1.census"
    grep '^worked: ' "$out/$1.census" > "$out/$1.out" || { echo "cost: $1 printed no worked line"; exit 1; }
}

# Each edit of the warm lane's table, over the store the cli check left.
warm_edits() {
    warm settle
    cp "$src/$edited" "$out/edited.orig"
    edits | while IFS='|' read -r kind text becomes; do
        [ -z "$text" ] || python3 "$root/tools/cost_ratchet.py" --edit "$src/$edited" "$kind" "$text" "$becomes"
        warm "edit-$kind"
        if [ -n "$text" ]; then
            cp "$out/edited.orig" "$src/$edited"
            warm "back-$kind"
        fi
    done
    find "$out/settle.out" "$out"/back-*.out -delete
}

bare() {
    find "$src" -path '*/.avra-cache*' -delete
    find "$src/packages" \( -path '*/src/main' -o -name '*.av.ll' \) -type f -delete
    mkdir -p "$cache"
    find "$cache" -mindepth 1 -delete
}

workloads | while read -r name command; do
    bare
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    counted "$name" $command
    [ "$name" != check-cli ] || warm_edits
done
find "$out/cache" "$src" "$out/edited.orig" -delete

**Where each rise comes from** (store pinned off, each merge measured with its own compiler, against cost56):
- **The measurement itself (defects, 2e56e49f).** The machine store is now on by default, and every cost run fills a store of its own. That alone accounts for about 6 points of build-cli's boxes (+16% → +10%) and about 3 points of check-cli's string_compares. Batch 57's `tools/cost.sh` doesn't pin the store off, and my batch-58 change doesn't either. Adding `AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=0` there is the lead's call, since it changes the gate.
- **The real regression (parity-values 2f240144, commit 2aef1bec).** This is most of the rest:
  - build-cli boxes +8.1%, reclaims +8.4%, list_writes +8.6%, retains +6.3%, about the same on check-cli.
  - All the warm rises: body, comment and literal +13, signature +12, inline +9.
  - The cause: each item's law checks now call `top_level_defined`, which isn't a query and reads every item in the file. Cold, that is items-squared work. Warm, one edit re-works the law checks of all 14 items in the file instead of 1.
  - I checked this against the per-query breakdown of the warm runs. It is genuinely more work, not the hash-order effect parallel-main found.
- **defects, 4d873bb0** (the `// LICENSED` id check): string_compares +6.7% on check-cli and +4.0% on check-program. build-cli doesn't move.

- **Small or harmless:**

**The fix under test.** I marked `top_level_defined` as `@cut_query`, the same pattern `records_with_field` uses in that file. If the cost run shows the 2aef1bec rows returning to cost56 and warm law checks back to one answer per edit, I'll tell the lead the fix is confirmed. content.text: I'll answer it from the `worked:` line itself. It breaks each warm run's answers down by query kind, so I can compare land57's breakdown with cost56's. New kinds appearing means new work. The same kinds with the same total split differently means the hash-order artifact.

message.content: Lead, input for your bisect: parallel-main found that warm `worked` counts depend on question-hash ORDER. The frontier decides its cuts in place order, sorted by hash, a question's hash includes the code hash of the lowered code it reaches, and so any change to reachable compiler code reorders which question owns a shared read. That moves warm rows (they saw 280 vs 286 from an equivalent reorder). So part of batch 57's warm rise may be this artifact rather than real work. When you attribute the warm rows, say whether each rise is more queries actually worked for the edit or the same work owned differently. The cold rows (boxes +16% and so on) aren't explained by this.

payload.result:
Batch 57's red cost slice is partly the measurement, not the compiler. I posted that to the lead; the per-merge bisect for the rest is running now.

**The measurement part.** Since defects (07a87adf), the machine store is on unless `AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=0`. land57's `tools/cost.sh` doesn't pin it off, so every cold run builds a store of std answers in its own cache. I ran `make cost` on land57 twice, as it stands and with the store pinned off. Over cost56:

| row | store as it stands | store off |
|---|---|---|
| build-cli boxes | +16.1% | +10.2% |
| build-cli reclaims | +16.6% | +10.5% |
| build-cli list_writes | +13.9% | +11.3% |
| check-cli string_compares | +10.6% | +7.5% |

**The compiler part.** Pinning the store off doesn't move these, so they come from the compiler:
- queries_computed: +4.0%
- warm edit-body, edit-comment and edit-literal: +14 answers each
- warm edit-inline: +10 answers

**The bisect.** It covers the 5 merges that can move a counter: 39823499, 07a87adf, a9c4598c, 2f240144, 5adb73cf. Each run uses that merge's own census compiler with the store pinned off, about 15 minutes per merge. land57 itself is already measured, and f28544ea and a2af0d93 only touch gate.sh. When it finishes I'll post per-row attribution, then narrow each rise to the commit inside its merge.

**Fix for the measurement.** cost.sh should set `AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=0`. I've left that to the lead because it changes the gate outside my own commits. My batch-58 change (3c20ba7f) isolates HOME and the cache but doesn't pin the store off either.

#!/bin/sh
# b57.sh <merge...>: each merge's census compiler (built by land57's gen-2) under `make cost`, the
# machine store pinned off, its counts to /tmp/claude-0/b57/<merge>/
set -u
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500
wt=/work/b57-wt
[ -e "$wt/.git" ] || git -C /work/avra worktree add -f --detach "$wt" land57 > /dev/null 2>&1
for m in "$@"; do

payload.result:
I'm bisecting batch 57's cost rises now, ahead of phase 2.

**Machine store, the lead's first question:** it is very likely part of the rise.
- defects (07a87adf) turned the machine store on unless `AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=0`. With no `AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR` set, the store sits in the run's own cache at `$AVRA_CACHE_DIR/tapes`.
- On first use it lays the toolchain's std answers into that store.
- land57's `tools/cost.sh` doesn't pin the store off. My HOME and store isolation only rides batch 58. So every cold and warm run in batch 57's cost slice now builds and reads a store of its own, which means the measurement changed rather than the compiler.

**How I'm testing it:**
- land57 gen-2 is building in `/work/l57-wt`.
- Then `make cost` runs twice: once as the harness stands, and once with `AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=0` from a scratch copy of cost.sh that I restore afterwards and never commit.
- If the store-off run lands back near cost56, the store is the cause.
- Anything left over gets bisected across the 6 merges with the store pinned off, so only the compiler varies.

**Merges that could own any residual:**
- spec-harness (39823499): adds item_rules and law_findings queries.
- parity-types (a9c4598c): item_new_only.
- parity-values (2f240144): item_annotations, item_generators.
- lowering-quality (5adb73cf): item_program, checking, tapes.av.
- laws-fusion (f4a1828f): item_decl_shapes. The string_compares price was already ruled for this one in batch 56.
- f28544ea and a2af0d93 change only gate.sh and can't move a counter.

I'll post per-row attribution once the two runs finish.

<to_controller>empty-literal opens: NOISE, measured. Going to phase 2 unless you overrule.
1. Cost of one open: 15.3 ns (open + push + release, C bench against libavra_runtime.a on 1 core, 37M iterations, 3 rounds). One box_alloc holds the header and 8 inline cells, and the mark bytes are zeroed. A fresh list sized for the push costs 11.7 ns. A fresh cap-0 list grown by its push costs 26.5 ns.
2. The open already is the lazy design: the immortal `[]` costs nothing until the first write, and that write makes exactly the one allocation a list born at its first push would make. No lowering can remove an allocation here. A list born empty and grown is worse (+11 ns).
3. Win ceiling: 3.6 ns (the is_shared → box_clone routing) × 37M = 0.13 s per cli build, about 0.07% of a ~200 s build. A runtime fast path in avra_cell_unique for the two static empties would remove most of it in about 5 lines, without touching the lowering.
4. The `empty_opens` row stays, so it ratchets, and the fresh-empty candidates still name sites where a list never needs to exist. Those are a deforestation question, which phase 2 covers.
5. Bundle 22752bc7 is unchanged (for batch 58). Phase 2 next: devirtualization (a census hook at each CallPtr) and deforestation (a walked-once label).</to_controller>

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Exact-count cost gate:
     - `make cost` runs tools/cost.sh and tools/cost_ratchet.py.
     - Tolerance is 0.05%.
     - An accept over the same snapshot never raises a row; raising rows needs `COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> make cost-accept`.
     - `tools/cost.candidates` is report-only.
   - Census compiler: tools/census_compiler.sh with `CENSUS_BUILDER`. The builder must sit inside the tree's build/, and the package objects must be built first.
   - Census env vars: AVRA_MEM_STATS, AVRA_CENSUS_SITES, AVRA_CENSUS_DEATHS, AVRA_CENSUS_TOP.
   - Gen-1 vs gen-2: a compiler built once from the standing e2bce925 binary traps on std-avrac with "a string holding a NUL crossed to C". Build twice before trusting std-avrac results. Cold builds need AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500.
   - Runtime copies:
     - `is_shared` answers true for immortal boxes, so the first write to `Cell.new([])` or `mut x = []` opens a clone of the empty static.
     - These are counted as copies but cost one allocation each.
   - Idioms gate: `check --baseline tools/idioms.baseline`, 0 NEW required. Rules hit: closures.pronoun_lambda (use `it`), compiler.duplicated_literal, compiler.one_body_arms (join arms with `or`).
   - A `match` over a nullable enum is refused; unwrap first with `let l? = ... else {}`.

       let call? = match i { .CallRtVoid(callee, args) or .CallRt(_, callee, args) -> RowCall { callee: callee, args: args }, rest -> null, } else { return [] }
       fn minted_record(...) { match i { .CallRt(dst, callee, _) -> if callee == "avra_array_sized" && record(layouts, dst) { [dst] } else { [] }, _ -> [], } }
       fn scalar(layouts: List<Layout>, r: Reg) -> bool {
           let l? = laid(layouts, r) else { return false }
           match l { .Word or .Real or .Truth -> true, .Void or .Boxed(_) or .Bare or .Fields(_) or .Tagged(_) or .Maybe(_) -> false, }

content.thinking: The cause is that a `.get()` in a function body holds its borrow until the function ends, so later writes copy whole columns: `ReadTable.added` copies `key_highs` and `slots` on every add, and `put` copies `part_words` per part read. I'm moving those bindings into a helper that returns before the write, as the helper rule requires.

+use answer_record.{AnswerRecord, ContentHash, PartSeen, RecordedRead}
+
+/// The words a part read keeps beside its row: its question's, then its part's name's and hash's.
+const PART_WORDS: int = 6
+
+/// THE READS A QUESTION MAKES, AS COLUMNS: a read is its key's two words, the two words of the whole
+/// answer it saw, and for a part read its question and the part's name and hash beside them; no read
+/// is a record until one is asked for. Keyed as a `HashKeyedTable` is.
+@identity
+export type ReadTable = {
+    key_highs: Cell<List<int>>,
+    key_lows: Cell<List<int>>,
+    answer_highs: Cell<List<int>>,
+    answer_lows: Cell<List<int>>,
+    /// Where a part read's words start among `part_words`; -1 for a whole read.
+    part_at: Cell<List<int>>,
+    part_words: Cell<List<int>>,
+    /// Each slot holds one more than a row, or zero when it's free.
+    slots: Cell<List<int>>,
+}
+
+export fn read_table() -> ReadTable {
+    let key_highs: Cell<List<int>> = Cell.new([])
+    let key_lows: Cell<List<int>> = Cell.new([])
+    let answer_highs: Cell<List<int>> = Cell.new([])
+    let answer_lows: Cell<List<int>> = Cell.new([])
+    let part_at: Cell<List<int>> = Cell.new([])
+    let part_words: Cell<List<int>> = Cell.new([])
+    let slots: Cell<List<int>> = Cell.new([])
+    ReadTable {
+        key_highs: key_highs,
+        key_lows: key_lows,
+        answer_highs: answer_highs,
+        answer_lows: answer_lows,
+        part_at: part_at,
+        part_words: part_words,
+        slots: slots,
+    }
+}
+
+impl ReadTable {
+    /// A read of the whole answer `answer` to the question known as `question`; one here already under
+    /// that question is this read after.
+    fn whole(question: ContentHash, answer: ContentHash) {
+        let row? = self.row_at(question.high_word, question.low_word) else {
+            return self.added(question.high_word, question.low_word, answer, -1)
+        }
+        self.answer_highs.set_at(row, answer.high_word)
+        self.answer_lows.set_at(row, answer.low_word)
+        self.part_at.set_at(row, -1)
+    }
+
+    /// `read`, kept under its key; one here already under that key is `read` after.
+    fn put(read: RecordedRead) {
+        let part? = read.part else { return self.whole(read.question, read.whole_answer) }
+        let key = read.read_key()
+        let at = self.part_words.get().length
+        for w in [
+            read.question.high_word,
+            read.question.low_word,
+            part.part_name.high_word,
+            part.part_name.low_word,
+            part.part_hash.high_word,
+            part.part_hash.low_word,
+        ] { self.part_words.push(w) }
+        let row? = self.row_at(key.high_word, key.low_word) else {
+            return self.added(key.high_word, key.low_word, read.whole_answer, at)
+        }
+        self.answer_highs.set_at(row, read.whole_answer.high_word)
+        self.answer_lows.set_at(row, read.whole_answer.low_word)
+        self.part_at.set_at(row, at)
+    }
+
+    /// The read kept under `key`, made a record; absent when there's none.
+    fn get(key: ContentHash) -> RecordedRead? {
+        let row? = self.row_at(key.high_word, key.low_word) else { return null }
+        self.read_at(row)
+    }
+
+    /// Every read, made records, in the order its key first arrived.
+    fn values() -> List<RecordedRead> { [self.read_at(row) for row in 0..self.key_highs.get().length] }
+
+    /// The question words of every read, two a read, in the order its key first arrived.
+    fn question_words() -> List<int> {
+        let parts = self.part_at.get()
+        let words = self.part_words.get()
+        let highs = self.key_highs.get()
+        let lows = self.key_lows.get()
+        mut out: List<int> = []
+        for row, at in parts {
+            out.push(if at < 0 { highs[row] } else { words[at] })
+            out.push(if at < 0 { lows[row] } else { words[at + 1] })
+        }
+        out
+    }
+
+    /// The record of `answer`, worked out with these reads: the whole reads' words, then the part
+    /// reads', as `answer_record` lays them.
+    fn record_of(answer: ContentHash) -> AnswerRecord {
+        let parts = self.part_at.get()
+        let words = self.part_words.get()
+        let highs = self.key_highs.get()
+        let lows = self.key_lows.get()
+        let answer_highs = self.answer_highs.get()
+        let answer_lows = self.answer_lows.get()
+        mut whole: List<int> = []
+        mut parted: List<int> = []
+        for row, at in parts {
+            if at < 0 {
+                whole.push(highs[row])
+                whole.push(lows[row])
+                whole.push(answer_highs[row])
+                whole.push(answer_lows[row])
+            } else {
+                parted.push(words[at])
+                parted.push(words[at + 1])
+                parted.push(answer_highs[row])
+                parted.push(answer_lows[row])
+                for k in at + 2..at + PART_WORDS { parted.push(words[k]) }

commit 451ad9b87316cfffee13f4f1e60cd75139c06a87
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   Thu Nov 19 04:12:03 2026 +0000

    The exact-count gate: every counter of fixed workloads held to its row
    
    `make cost` (the `cost` gate slice; keepers-a1) builds the census compiler
    of the tree and runs it over one pinned commit of the sources: a cold cli
    check, a cold cli build and a cold std-program check, each census counter
    held to tools/cost.baseline within 0.05%; and the answers a warm
    `tapes --findings` of the cli works out again after each edit of the warm
    lane's set, held the same way. One process on one core does all the work,
    every run starts bare, and nothing is read inside the stamp window, so a
    check's counts repeat exactly. A row only falls, through `make
    cost-accept`; `COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> make cost-accept` moves the snapshot.
    It replaces census-gate and tools/census.budget. The census runtime totals
    copies and string compares.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01F8zAGdAmJ7HHi46XYh8si9

+static int64_t g_copies, g_streqs;

#!/bin/sh
# probe.sh <commit> [workload...]: the census compiler of <commit>, run cold over snapshot d5062c32
# on the named workloads (default check-program), counts to /tmp/claude-0/bis/<sha8>/<w>.out
set -u
c=$(git -C /work/avra rev-parse --short=8 "$1"); shift
ws=${*:-check-program}
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500
wt=/work/bis-wt
out=/tmp/claude-0/bis/$c
mkdir -p "$out"
[ -e "$wt/.git" ] || git -C /work/avra worktree add -f --detach "$wt" "$c" > /dev/null 2>&1
cd "$wt" || exit 2
git checkout -q -f --detach "$c" || exit 2
git clean -q -f -d -e build/ > /dev/null
mkdir -p build
[ -x "$out/avra.census" ] || {
    cp /work/b55-wt/build/avra-lane build/avra-lane
    make --no-print-directory $(make -pn 2> /dev/null | awk -F' := |= ' '/^PACKAGE_OBJS/{print $2; exit}') > "$out/objs.log" 2>&1
    s=$(date +%s)
    CENSUS_BUILDER=build/avra-lane sh tools/census_compiler.sh "$out/avra.census" > "$out/census.log" 2>&1 || { tail -5 "$out/census.log"; echo "probe $c: no census compiler"; exit 1; }
    echo "probe $c: census compiler $(($(date +%s) - s)) s"
}
src=/work/bis-src
cache=/work/bis-cache
if [ ! -d "$src/packages" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$src/build"
    git -C /work/avra archive d5062c32741cba87a5cb7964cb86e0a2768d5c1a | tar -x -C "$src"
fi
cp "$out/avra.census" "$src/build/avra"
find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name 'avra_hot.bc' -o -name 'avra_hot.inc' \) -exec cp {} "$src/build/" \;
for w in $ws; do
    case $w in
        check-program) cmd="check --counts packages/std-program" ;;
        check-cli) cmd="check --counts packages/cli" ;;
        build-cli) cmd="build packages/cli" ;;
    esac
    find "$src" -path '*/.avra-cache*' -delete
    find "$src/packages" \( -path '*/src/main' -o -name '*.av.ll' \) -type f -delete
    mkdir -p "$cache/home"; find "$cache" -mindepth 1 -delete; mkdir -p "$cache/home"
    sleep 3
    s=$(date +%s)
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    (cd "$src" && unset AVRA_MACHINE_STORE AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR && \
        HOME="$cache/home" AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 \
        taskset -c 0 build/avra $cmd > "$out/$w.stdout" 2> "$out/$w.out") || { tail -5 "$out/$w.out"; echo "probe $c: $w failed"; }
    echo "probe $c: $w $(($(date +%s) - s)) s"
done

# One run of the census compiler in the snapshot, once what it reads is older than the stamp window:

        fi

tool_use_result.originalFile:
# Zero cost — the registry

The law (CLAUDE.md, "PERFORMANT BY DEFAULT"): idiomatic code IS the fast code. A writer never
hand-tunes a representation; the compiler chooses it, and the cost of what was written is visible
and gated. This file is the registry the law is held to: one row per technique, each with the
DETECTOR that finds its candidates. A technique without a detector is a wish, not a row.

## Detectors — how candidates are found

Four instruments, each reading what the compiler or the runtime already knows (P10). None is a
human reading code.

| detector | reads | finds | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| **census sites** | the runtime's exact per-site counters (boxes, retains, releases, clones, string compares, list writes) over the fixed workloads | the hottest sites, each CLASSIFIED to the technique that would remove its cost (below) | `avra census --candidates` |
| **missed-optimization remarks** | the compiler at the moment a technique declines to fire | WHY a site paid: "record escapes through a field write at X, so it is boxed" | `avra explain cost <fn>`; the remarks are facts in the DB |
| **shape rules** | the source, as `rule` declarations `avra check` finds | the patterns that cost by construction | `avra check`, ratcheted like idioms |
| **exact-count gate** | the census totals per cold workload, and the answers a warm run works out again after each fixed edit, over one pinned snapshot, against `tools/cost.baseline` | regressions: any counter that rose past tolerance, cold or warm | a gate slice (`make cost`); lowering a counter needs `make cost-accept` |

**The classifier** is what makes candidates automatic. A census site's SHAPE names its technique:

| site shape (from the census) | technique |
|---|---|
| a box freed in the fn that made it | stack records (escape analysis) |
| a free at rc 1 followed by an alloc of the same size | reuse in place |
| a retain whose release is the binding's last use | move at last use |
| `avra_streq`/name compare callers | interned names |
| a box of flat scalar fields pushed into a list | strided list |
| a slot box over a crossed box (`F?`) | nullable flat record |
| a list made and only walked once | deforestation |
| an indirect call whose target set is one fn | devirtualization |
| a `dyn` box laid with N code pointers | static method tables |

`avra census --candidates` prints the top sites per technique with their counts and the source
line, so a ranked work list is one command. Run per batch on the gate's workloads, its output
diffed against the last run is how a NEW candidate appears without anyone looking.

## How work is assessed

- **Every PR**: the exact-count gate holds; a new shape-rule finding fails like an idiom.
- **Every new feature**: its design post names its cost (boxes, calls, copies per use) and which
  registry rows it relies on or adds. A feature that makes idiomatic code slower needs a row that
  removes the cost, or it is not ready.
- **Maintenance**: a finding from any detector is a row or a ticket at discovery, never a comment.
- **New techniques** join this table with their detector in the same change.

## Techniques

| technique | status | removes |
|---|---|---|
| packed lists of scalars | landed (batch 48) | a mark byte a cell, boxes per element |
| strided lists of flat records | in progress (alloc) | a box per element |
| nullable flat record as presence + words | designed (alloc (2), after the aggregate rewrite) | 2 boxes per `F?` |
| static method tables | done (lowering-quality, to land) | N code-pointer pushes per `dyn` box: one table per type and trait, laid once as data; a box is its value and its table |
| aggregates as leaf scalars, unfilled parts zeroed | in progress (parallel-main) | SelectionDAG fallbacks, undef words |
| release rows | landed (batch 48) | release call sites |
| interned names | proposed | string compares in lookups |
| reuse in place (Perceus/FBIP) | proposed | free + alloc pairs |
| move at last use (borrow inference) | partial (params' consumes) | retain/release pairs |
| devirtualization | proposed | indirect calls with one target |
| deforestation | partial (walk chains) | intermediate lists |
| scalar replacement / stack records | proposed | boxes that never escape |
| arenas per query | proposed | per-temporary frees |
| set/switch lowering of `x in [literals]` | proposed | linear scans over constants |
| column layout for List<Record> read by field | proposed | strided reads of one field |

input.new_string:
line, so a ranked work list is one command. Run per batch on the gate's workloads, its output
diffed against the last run is how a NEW candidate appears without anyone looking.

`make cost` runs every workload with the site tables on, resolves each site to its symbol and
writes `build/cost/candidates.txt` (`avra census --candidates [--root <tree>] <report>…`, the top

content.content:
| **exact-count gate** | the census totals per cold workload, and the answers a warm run works out again after each fixed edit, over one pinned snapshot, against `tools/cost.baseline` | regressions: any counter that rose past tolerance, cold or warm | a gate slice (`make cost`); lowering a counter needs `make cost-accept` |

**The classifier** is what makes candidates automatic. A census site's SHAPE names its technique:

| site shape (from the census) | technique |
|---|---|
| a box freed in the fn that made it | stack records (escape analysis) |
| a free at rc 1 followed by an alloc of the same size | reuse in place |
| a retain whose release is the binding's last use | move at last use |
| `avra_streq`/name compare callers | interned names |
| a box of flat scalar fields pushed into a list | strided list |
| a slot box over a crossed box (`F?`) | nullable flat record |
| a list made and only walked once | deforestation |
| an indirect call whose target set is one fn | devirtualization |
| a `dyn` box laid with N code pointers | static method tables |

`avra census --candidates` prints the top sites per technique with their counts and the source
line, so a ranked work list is one command. Run per batch on the gate's workloads, its output
diffed against the last run is how a NEW candidate appears without anyone looking.

## How work is assessed

- **Every PR**: the exact-count gate holds; a new shape-rule finding fails like an idiom.
- **Every new feature**: its design post names its cost (boxes, calls, copies per use) and which
  registry rows it relies on or adds. A feature that makes idiomatic code slower needs a row that
  removes the cost, or it is not ready.
- **Maintenance**: a finding from any detector is a row or a ticket at discovery, never a comment.
- **New techniques** join this table with their detector in the same change.

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}
trap shipping EXIT INT TERM
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without the census, so an inlined retain would count nothing.
# THE MINTED BOXES ARE NAMED: each box a runtime row makes is counted by
# its type (AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES), the `type:` table.
# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK: the old path's check the net runs first is not that work.
AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \
    "$builder" build packages/cli > build/census-build.out 2>&1 || {
    tail -20 build/census-build.out; echo "census: the census compiler did not build"; exit 1; }
# A BINARY THE PROGRAM LAYER PLACES IS ITS KEPT BINARY, LINKED: a census compiler left from an earlier
# run can be that same file, which `mv` will not move onto itself — the old one goes first.
[ ! -e "$out" ] || find "$out" -delete
mv packages/cli/src/main "$out"
# A C symbol wears a leading underscore on macOS and none on Linux.
nm "$out" | grep -Eq '[ _]note_retain$' || { echo "census: $out carries no census — refusing to report"; exit 1; }

index 00000000..0d1af49c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/backend/strided_census.av
@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@
+//! THE STRIDED CENSUS: a record box a body mints, fills with scalars alone and pushes into a list —
+//! a census build's label (`flat-pushed`), never a rule: what a strided list would hold in place of
+//! a box per element. Read beside the frame census, whose tags a label carries with it.
+use core.{Ins, Reg, Layout, RtSig}
+
+/// The census label tags of the boxes minted in `ins`, by register: the frame census's, and
+/// `flat-pushed` where a record of scalars is pushed into a list.
+export fn census_tags(ins: List<Ins>, layouts: List<Layout>, rt: Map<string, RtSig>) -> Map<
+    string,
+    string,
+> {
+    mut tags = frame_tags(ins, layouts, rt)
+    for key in flat_pushed(ins, layouts) {
+        let frame = tags.get(key)
+        tags.set(key, if frame == null { FLAT_PUSHED } else { "${frame!} ${FLAT_PUSHED}" })
+    }
+    tags
+}
+
+/// The tag of a record of scalars pushed into a list.
+const FLAT_PUSHED: string = "flat-pushed"
+
+/// Each record box `ins` mints whose every push into it is a scalar and that a push hands to a list,
+/// by its register's index.
+fn flat_pushed(ins: List<Ins>, layouts: List<Layout>) -> List<string> {
+    let records = [dst.index for i in ins for dst in minted_record(i, layouts)]
+    let pushes = [p for i in ins for p in pushed(i)]
+    ["${r}" for r in records if pushes.any((p) -> p.into == r) &&
+        pushes.all((p) -> p.into != r || scalar(layouts, p.value)) &&
+        pushes.any((p) -> p.value.index == r)]
+}
+
+/// One push: the list or record it writes into, and the value.
+type Push = { into: int, value: Reg }
+
+/// The push `i` makes, if it is one.
+fn pushed(i: Ins) -> List<Push> {
+    let call? = match i {
+        .CallRtVoid(callee, args) -> RowCall { callee: callee, args: args },
+        .CallRt(_, callee, args) -> RowCall { callee: callee, args: args },
+        rest -> null,
+    } else { return [] }
+    if !call.callee.starts_with("avra_array_push") || call.args.length != 2 { return [] }
+    [Push { into: call.args[0].index, value: call.args[1] }]
+}
+
+/// A runtime row's call: its name and what it is handed.
+type RowCall = { callee: string, args: List<Reg> }
+
+/// The record box `i` mints, if it mints one.
+fn minted_record(i: Ins, layouts: List<Layout>) -> List<Reg> {
+    match i {
+        .CallRt(dst, callee, _) -> if callee == "avra_array_sized" && laid_as(layouts, dst) == "box record" { [dst] } else { [] },
+        rest -> [],
+    }
+}
+
+/// Whether `r` holds a scalar: a word, a float or a truth.
+fn scalar(layouts: List<Layout>, r: Reg) -> bool {
+    let laid = laid_as(layouts, r)
+    laid == "word" || laid == "real" || laid == "truth"
+}
+
+/// How `r` is laid, as the IR spells it; empty where no layout stands for it.
+fn laid_as(layouts: List<Layout>, r: Reg) -> string { if r.index < layouts.length { layouts[r.index].spelled() } else { "" } }

    pinned, base = read_baseline(text)
    now = measured(run_dir)
    if not now:
        print("cost: the run printed no counts — refusing to judge")
        return 1
    missing = unprinted(now)
    if missing:
        print("\n".join(missing))
        return 1
    if argv[1] == "--accept":
        same = ran == pinned
        if same:
            failed, _ = judge(now, base)
            if failed:
                print("\n".join(failed))
                print("cost: an accept never raises a row over the same snapshot")
                return 1
        open(BASELINE, "w").write(render(ran, accepted(now, base, same)))
        candidates_said(run_dir, True)
        print("cost: tools/cost.baseline recorded (snapshot %s)" % ran)
        return 0
    if ran != pinned:
        print("cost: the run measured snapshot %s, the baseline pins %s" % (ran, pinned))
        return 1
    failed, fell = judge(now, base)
    for line in fell + failed:
        print(line)
    print("cost: %d rows, %d over, %d fell" % (len(base), len(failed), len(fell)))
    candidates_said(run_dir, False)
    return 1 if failed else 0


def self_test():
    rows_lib.self_test()
    run = ("rc: 100 retains, 90 releases, 10 reclaims\nrc: 5 empty lists made, 1 grown\n"
           "rc: 1000 list reads, 200 list writes\nalloc: 50 boxes, 7 list buffers\n"
           "rc: 3 copies, 4 string compares\nmem: noise\n")
    got = counts_of(run)
    assert got == {"retains": 100, "releases": 90, "reclaims": 10, "empty_lists": 5, "empty_grown": 1,
                   "list_reads": 1000, "list_writes": 200, "boxes": 50, "list_buffers": 7,
                   "copies": 3, "string_compares": 4}, got
    assert set(got) == set(CENSUS)
    assert counts_of("counts: files_loaded=3 queries_computed=41 store_rows_written=41\n") == {"queries_computed": 41}
    assert counts_of("worked: 69 answers here; item_under 14\n") == {"worked": 69}
    # a noop's row of 0 fails at the first answer worked again
    assert judge({("edit-noop", "worked"): 1}, {("edit-noop", "worked"): 0})[0]
    # a fall inside the build's own jitter is not named
    assert judge({("w", "boxes"): 999_951}, {("w", "boxes"): 1_000_000}) == ([], [])
    # an edit stands once or is refused; a rename reaches every whole word and no part of one
    assert edited("a\nb\n", "body", "b", "c\\nd") == "a\nc\nd\n"
    for bad in ("x", "a"):
        try:
            edited("a a\n", "body", bad, "y")
            assert False, bad
        except ValueError:
            pass
    assert edited("f(x) f fg\n", "rename", "f", "g") == "g(x) g fg\n"
    sha = "a" * 40
    snap, rows = read_baseline(render(sha, {("w", "boxes"): 1000, ("w", "retains"): 10}))
    assert snap == sha and rows == {("w", "boxes"): 1000, ("w", "retains"): 10}
    # within the tolerance passes; one box past it fails, naming both numbers
    assert judge({("w", "boxes"): 100_050}, {("w", "boxes"): 100_000}) == ([], [])
    failed, _ = judge({("w", "boxes"): 100_051}, {("w", "boxes"): 100_000})
    assert failed == ["cost: w boxes: 100000 -> 100051 (+0.051%, over the 0.05% tolerance)"], failed
    # a fall passes and is named; a missing count fails
    failed, fell = judge({("w", "boxes"): 900}, {("w", "boxes"): 1000})
    assert failed == [] and "fell: 1000 -> 900" in fell[0]
    failed, _ = judge({}, {("w", "boxes"): 1000})
    assert "printed no count" in failed[0]
    # an accept over the same snapshot never raises; over another, it records what was measured
    assert accepted({("w", "boxes"): 1004}, {("w", "boxes"): 1000}, True) == {("w", "boxes"): 1000}
    assert accepted({("w", "boxes"): 900}, {("w", "boxes"): 1000}, True) == {("w", "boxes"): 900}
    assert accepted({("w", "boxes"): 1200}, {("w", "boxes"): 1000}, False) == {("w", "boxes"): 1200}
    assert unprinted({("edit-body", "worked"): 3}) == []
    assert unprinted({("check-cli", "queries_computed"): 3})[0] == "cost: check-cli printed no retains"
    # a candidate is keyed by its technique and fn; one the record lacks is said, by its line
    found = candidates_of("candidate: reuse-in-place 40 f packages/x.av:3\ncandidate: strided-list 9 g packages/y.av\n")
    assert set(found) == {("reuse-in-place", "f"), ("strided-list", "g")}
    assert recorded("# head\nreuse-in-place f\n") == {("reuse-in-place", "f")}
    assert new_candidates(found, {("reuse-in-place", "f")}) == ["cost: new candidate: strided-list 9 g packages/y.av"]
    print("cost_ratchet self-test: ok")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

#!/bin/sh
# Measure the cost and determinism of census workloads.
#   census_measure.sh build            build the census compiler once, timed
#   census_measure.sh run <tag> <ahead:on|off> <cmd...>   one cold run, timed, counts saved
set -u
T=/work/avra
SRC=/work/census-src
OUT=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/eabfde80-5d84-5793-ab10-2655cf2de6a7/scratchpad/census
mkdir -p "$OUT"
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
case "$1" in
build)
    cd "$T"
    counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
    if [ -n "${SITES:-}" ]; then export AVRA_CENSUS_SITES=1; fi
    s=$(date +%s)
    make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > "$OUT/rt.out" 2>&1 || { tail -5 "$OUT/rt.out"; exit 1; }
    m=$(date +%s)
    AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \
        /usr/bin/time -f "build: %e s wall, %U s user, %M KB peak" build/avra-try build packages/cli > "$OUT/build.out" 2>&1
    rc=$?
    e=$(date +%s)
    [ $rc -eq 0 ] && cp packages/cli/src/main build/avra.census-gate
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2>/dev/null
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || echo "shipping runtime did not rebuild"
    f=$(date +%s)
    echo "runtime $((m-s)) s; compiler build $((e-m)) s (rc $rc); runtime restore $((f-e)) s"
    tail -1 "$OUT/build.out"
    nm build/avra.census-gate | grep -Eq '[ _]note_retain$' && echo "census binary ok"
    ;;
run)
    tag=$2; ahead=$3; shift 3
    cache=/tmp/census-cache-fixed; [ -d "$cache" ] && find "$cache" -delete; mkdir -p "$cache"
    cd "$SRC"
    find "$SRC/packages" \( -path "*/src/main" -o -name "*.av.ll" \) -type f -delete 2>/dev/null
    find "$SRC" -path "*/.avra-cache*" -delete 2>/dev/null
    if [ "$ahead" = off ]; then export AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1; else unset AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF; fi
    if [ -n "${SITES:-}" ]; then export AVRA_CENSUS_SITES=1; fi
    s=$(date +%s)
    AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 \
        /usr/bin/time -f "time: %e s wall, %U s user, %M KB peak" "$T/build/avra.census-gate" "$@" > "$OUT/$tag.stdout" 2> "$OUT/$tag.out"
    rc=$?
    e=$(date +%s)
    grep -E '^(rc:|alloc: [0-9]|once:|time:)' "$OUT/$tag.out" > "$OUT/$tag.counts"
    echo "$tag rc=$rc $((e-s)) s"; cat "$OUT/$tag.counts"
    find "$cache" -delete
    find "$SRC" -path "*/.avra-cache*" -delete 2>/dev/null
    ;;
esac

# Handoff — lane `avra-lane-parity-wrong-answers`

Branch and file stem must be exactly `avra-lane-parity-wrong-answers`
(bundle sent as `/work/avra-lane-parity-wrong-answers.bundle`). Repo: `/work/avra`.

## Scope (as the lead set it, in order of arrival)

1. Parity: wrong answers and traps of the program layer vs the old path (`AVRA_PROGRAM=0`),
   RUN-ONLY programs, `type.struct_fields`, and a tail list of unheld "B" kinds — DONE up to
   batch 45c; the remaining tail singles are PARKED by the lead.
2. **The exact-count gate** (`make cost`, gate slice `cost`) — DONE, landed as one commit.
3. **`avra census --candidates`** (docs/ZERO_COST.md's classifier), phase 1 = techniques 1–7 —
   IN FLIGHT (WIP commit).

Kinds held by OTHER lanes (never take): lambda, variant_lit, unknown_prop, match, pattern (values);
mismatch (types); method, list_element, variant_arity, the `{}` map-verb voice (resolve-2); spread,
seat, list, alias_copy, record_pattern, spread_nullable, component_event (layer-commands); words /
false-refusals (C); the three arity traps (parity-types).

## Base

`batch53` = `d5062c32741cba87a5cb7964cb86e0a2768d5c1a` (from `/work/batch53.bundle`, prerequisite
d750dfa7). Every earlier commit of this lane has landed inside batch 53.

## Commits ahead of batch53

- `451ad9b8` The exact-count gate: every counter of fixed workloads held to its row — SENT to the
  lead (bundle batch53..451ad9b8), receipts all green, `GATE cost PASS` 42 rows 0 over 0 fell.
- `d56b77e5` WIP: avra census --candidates, phase 1 (techniques 1-7), and the cost gate's hardening —
  NOT sent, NOT through receipts.

`/work/handoff/lane.bundle` = `avra-lane-parity-wrong-answers ^batch53` (both commits).
`/work/handoff/uncommitted.patch` is empty (nothing uncommitted).

## The exact-count gate (landed design, for orientation)

- `tools/cost.sh`: builds the census compiler (`tools/census_compiler.sh`, builder `CENSUS_BUILDER`,
  default `build/avra`), `git archive`s the pinned snapshot (`snapshot` row of `tools/cost.baseline`)
  into `build/cost/src`, puts the census compiler at `src/build/avra` (so std resolves INSIDE the
  snapshot) plus the build's `*.o/*.a/avra_hot.*`, and runs, each cold, bare, one core
  (`taskset -c 0`), `AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1`, `sleep 3` first (io.stamp's 2 s window):
  `check --counts packages/cli`, then the warm edits over its store, then `build packages/cli`,
  `check --counts packages/std-program`.
- Warm rows: the warm lane's `count.py` protocol exactly (`tapes --findings packages/cli`,
  `worked:` line, 8 edits of `cli/src/commands/cache.av`, each edit then a warm-back run).
- `tools/cost_ratchet.py`: tolerance 0.05% (lead's ruling), falls reported past 0.005%; accept only
  lowers rows over the same snapshot; `COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> make cost-accept` moves the snapshot and
  records everything. `--edit` applies one edit; `--self-test`.
- Determinism (proven): checks and warm rows IDENTICAL run to run; cold build ±4 retains/±14 list
  reads (a file it writes and reads back inside the stamp window). Fixes that were needed: one core
  (emit forks one process per core otherwise and the census counts the parent only), clearing the
  build's leftover product binary (+86 boxes otherwise), `AVRA_MEM_STATS=1` (no report without it).
- Baseline: batch53's compiler over snapshot d5062c32 (lead: it carries a regression being bisected;
  the fix lowers the rows through cost-accept). Bisect: `COST_COMPILER=<census compiler of X>
  sh tools/cost.sh && python3 tools/cost_ratchet.py --judge build/cost`.
- Slice cost ≈ 17 min (census compiler 2.5 + cli check 4.6 + warm 3.5 + build 5.5 + program 0.6);
  with the candidate tables on, ≈ +18%. CI keepers job limit is 30 min — watch it.

## In flight: `avra census --candidates` (WIP commit d56b77e5)

Done in the commit:
- runtime (census-only, `runtime/avra_runtime.c`, `avra_hot.c/.h`): `streq:` site table (avra_streq
  callers), `move:` pairs (a retain then the release of that box with no rc op between; `note_retain(box,
  site)`/`note_release(box, site)`), `reuse:` pairs (a free — set in `death_noted`, needs
  AVRA_CENSUS_DEATHS=1 — then the next alloc of the same size_row, in `note_made`), generic `pair_in` /
  `report_pairs`. Compiles with and without -DAVRA_CENSUS.
- backend: `compiler/backend/strided_census.av` — `census_tags` = frame tags + `flat-pushed` on a
  record minted by `avra_array_sized`, filled by `avra_array_push*` of word/real/truth values only, and
  pushed into a list; `llvm.av` uses `census_tags`.
- cli: `packages/cli/src/commands/census.av` — `avra census --candidates [--root <tree>] <report>…`;
  registered in `main.av`. Prints `candidate: <technique> <count> <fn> <file>:<line>`, top 10 per
  technique; symbols `av_…$XX…` decoded; fn line found in the file under `--root`. Tested by hand
  (all 7 kinds, summing, pair-of-two-fns skipped, missing report → exit 1).
- `tools/cost.sh`: every run with `AVRA_CENSUS_SITES=1 AVRA_CENSUS_DEATHS=1 AVRA_CENSUS_TOP=1000000`,
  own empty `HOME`, `AVRA_MACHINE_STORE(_DIR)` unset; `resolved()` rewrites each cold run's site lines
  to symbols (`<w>.sites`, addr2line on `src/build/avra`); writes `build/cost/candidates.txt`.
- `tools/cost_ratchet.py`: `candidates_said` — prints `cost: new candidate: …` for each
  (technique, fn) not in `tools/cost.candidates` (REPORT-ONLY, lead's permanent ruling), and the
  accept writes that file.

How far: a full `CENSUS_BUILDER=build/avra-try make cost` with a fresh census compiler was running
at handoff (started 08:46, log `/tmp/cost-cand.log`, outputs in `build/cost/`). The cold cli check had
finished: tables populated (54,231 site lines; 7,919 move/reuse/streq; 6 `flat-pushed` sites), and
its counters were +1,210 boxes / +1,810 retains over the batch53 baseline (≈1e-6, within 0.05%, NOT
identical). Likely cause, unproven: the census compiler now runs the strided tag pass while compiling
the snapshot (census types are on in that binary), i.e. real extra compiler work, not noise.

## Next 3 items, in order

1. Finish the proof run: `CENSUS_BUILDER=build/avra-try make cost` must say 0 over (rises ≤ 0.05%
   pass). Confirm the +1e-6 drift is the strided pass (e.g. compare a census compiler built without
   `census_tags`' flat_pushed). If it is, record it (`make cost-accept` over the same snapshot cannot
   raise rows — so either leave the baseline as is, since it passes, or ask the lead whether to
   re-record). Check `build/cost/candidates.txt` looks right (≤ 10 per technique, real file:line).
2. Write `tools/cost.candidates` from that run (`python3 tools/cost_ratchet.py --accept build/cost`
   writes it, and also lowers rows — only acceptable if no row fell for a spurious reason), then turn
   the WIP into a proper commit (message without "WIP", idioms `check packages/std-avrac` and
   `packages/cli` with `--baseline tools/idioms.baseline`, fmt), add `avra census` to docs/ZERO_COST.md
   if needed, run full receipts, bundle `batch53..HEAD` (or newest batch), post ≤ 12 lines.
3. Phase 2 of the classifier: deforestation (a list made and walked once — needs per-list read counts
   at death) and devirtualization (an indirect call with one target — needs a census hook at each
   `CallPtr` in emitted code). Then the parked tail singles if the lead re-opens them.

## Open rulings / asks waiting on others

- None blocking. Given: tolerance 0.05%; one commit; baseline at batch53's compiler; candidates
  report-only permanently; the warm rows (all work, one process) are the measure, and the warm lane
  re-bases its design budgets on them (lead told it).
- Parked: `table<int>` / literal under an owned type — wait for parity-resolve-2's voice "`X` is a
  type the language owns; a record literal can't make one" to land, then check it once (layer must
  say it for int/float/…/ptr/void/Bytes/Range; pin known-to-differ vs the old path's wrong words).
- Tail singles left (parked by the lead): param_default in a trait, `Self` in a trait static fn,
  map_entry ×2, within ×2, select, spent_arm, chain, propagate, applied, binding (dyn), catch,
  coalesce_never, impl, infer_result, interp_hole, list_scalar, task_escape, type_value, unread_mark,
  resolve.unresolved `let x = Bytes`, the order-only ones need nothing. Program sets: `/tmp/bk/<kind>/<n>/x.av`
  (lost with the container; regenerate from `/work/split-736.tsv`).

## Rules this lane works under (lead's, verbatim essentials)

- Commit as you go; push NOWHERE (no git push, no gh); never print/post credentials.
- No `rm` (use `find … -delete`), no `git stash`, no `git reset --hard`, no `--no-verify`.
- Fix root causes; declarative, general code; comments evergreen and terse; a law never assembles
  prose (named voice fns, shared with the old path via `said_as`); idioms baseline 0 NEW.
- One heavy job at a time (15 GB machine); never end a turn with a build running; one foreground wait,
  no polling loops of many turns.
- TOKEN RULE: post only at a bundle, a blocker or a ruling; ≤ 12 lines, numbers first.
- Every bundle's receipts: layer `AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500 build/avra-try check packages/std-avrac`
  exit 0; idioms 0 NEW; `sh tools/gate.sh avrac-a`…`avrac-g` and `refusal-a/b/c` all PASS with no
  unpinned failure (and now `sh tools/gate.sh cost`). A gate red not from your own commits is REPORTED
  to the lead, never fixed.
- Commit trailer: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` and
  `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01F8zAGdAmJ7HHi46XYh8si9`. Never name the model in
  commit text beyond that trailer.
- Bridge: `mcp__claude-bridge__post_to_controller` / `send_files` with the session token the new
  account's bridge note gives (this one's was `cse_01F8zAGdAmJ7HHi46XYh8si9.32a2bad420dad2fe0579`).

## Things a fresh session trips on

- `. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh` first (LLVM 22, `AVRA_CAP_MB=12000`, `AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB=12000`).
- `make try` builds `build/avra-try` (the compiler of the tree); `build/avra` may be older — use
  `CENSUS_BUILDER=build/avra-try` for cost runs unless `make avra` was run. `build/avra.census` is the
  last census compiler (built from d56b77e5's tree) — `COST_COMPILER=build/avra.census` skips 2.5 min,
  but rebuild it after any runtime/backend change.
- `tools/cost.sh` needs `taskset` (Linux) and `git` objects for the snapshot sha (it fetches by sha in a
  shallow clone).
- The census report needs `AVRA_MEM_STATS=1`; site/pair tables need `AVRA_CENSUS_SITES=1`, `reuse:`
  needs `AVRA_CENSUS_DEATHS=1`; census binaries have no line tables (addr2line gives fn only).
- Refusal witnesses: `tools/program-refusals/<case>/`; pin helper `parity-wrong-answers/pin.sh <case>
  <source>` then `PIN=1 sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra-try <case>`; known-to-differ =
  a `differs.why` file.
- Python edit scripts: write them with the Write tool and run `python3 -I <file>`; nested heredocs in
  one shell command broke twice.
- `List.reverse()` is refused by the language; `read_text(p) catch null` does not make a nullable.
- Helper scripts copied to `/work/handoff/parity-wrong-answers/`: `receipts.sh` (all receipts in one
  background job), `census_measure.sh` (the determinism measurements), `pin.sh`, and
  `lambda_fnless.patch` (already landed as 39f6db76; kept for reference only).
- Scratch worktrees: `/work/base-wt` (detached, used for baselines), `/work/census-src` (an old
  plain export, safe to delete).

## How work lands

The single source for the landing path, Sprites, the watcher and the
CI gates is `docs/2026_10_11_THE_PIPELINE.md`; the section below is the
doctrine it expands.

- ALL WORK MOVES THROUGH SEVEN COMMANDS, and nothing else touches main:

      sh tools/work new <name>   # a worktree ../avra-<name> off main, and its Sprite
      sh tools/work run <cmd>    # run it on a GitHub runner (--sprite: the lane's Sprite), its exit status
      sh tools/work test         # what this branch touches, on this lane's Sprite
      sh tools/work land         # push, PR, arm auto-merge — no Sprite involved
      sh tools/work status       # PRs and their merge state; each lane and its Sprite
      sh tools/work sprites      # every Sprite at a glance; `--fix [name]` repairs
      sh tools/work unbind       # end this lane's run, free its Sprite, keep the worktree
      sh tools/work done --remove-worktree   # remove this lane too: ONLY with the owner's say-so

  Main lives on GitHub (avra-lang/avra): squash merges, linear history,
  no direct pushes. It requires the `test` check AND that a branch be up
  to date with it, and auto-merge lands a green, current PR by itself,
  one at a time. A local main
  only follows `origin/main` (the reference-transaction hook refuses any
  other update; a deliberate repair sets `AVRA_MAIN_OVERRIDE="<reason>"`).
- THE PR IS THE TRAIN, AND THERE IS NO MERGE QUEUE (dropped 2026-10-11:
  its only real value was testing `main` plus every PR ahead, which
  "require up to date" gives back for free one PR at a time, while the
  queue cost trains that tested many PRs at once — one red suite killed
  them all — HEADGREEN batching and a rebase treadmill). A PR's `test`
  check IS the gate, on the PR's own tree (`.github/workflows/
  checks.yml`): fmt on its changed `.av`, idioms and suites over the
  packages it TOUCHES, the compiler-dependent keepers, the seed check and
  the affected packages' suites; a PR that touches no `.av`, no package
  and no compiler source builds nothing. Before it builds anything it
  runs the keepers that need NO COMPILER (`make keepers-static`, half a
  minute), so a refusal one of them speaks stops on the PR. Because the
  branch must be up to date, the tree it tests already holds `main`, so a
  cross-PR interaction (two individually-green PRs
  colliding on a latent bug) is caught on the later PR's own run. THE
  COMPILER IS CACHED BY
  ITS OWN SOURCE (`tools/compiler_paths.sh`): a tree whose compiler is
  main's takes main's binary; otherwise the newest cached binary builds
  the tree twice (the generation law), and one too old to read it — new
  syntax, a new refusal about its own source — fails that build and the
  tree BOOTSTRAPS from the committed seed. Main's own push run caches
  the compiler every run starts from.
- A LANE ITERATES WITH `make try`, NEVER `make avra`: it builds the
  compiler with the STANDING `build/avra` into `build/avra-try` and never
  replaces the builder, so its store stays warm (a leaf edit, ~4 s held
  464/466) and `./avra-try <cmd>` probes the change. `make avra` is for
  a change the compiler must READ to build itself — codegen, the front
  end, a refusal about its own source — and before landing.
- A PRE-COMMIT HOOK refuses staged `.av` that is not canonical; the fix
  it prints is `build/avra fmt --write <files>`. Never `--no-verify`.
- HEAVY RUNS GO ON SPRITES, ONE SPRITE A LANE: `sh tools/work run <cmd>`
  from inside the worktree. `work new` binds a free Sprite (`work bind`
  for a worktree that has none, `work unbind` frees it), and the lane's
  tree and compiler stay warm there between runs. Bootstraps, whole
  suites and censuses run there; the Mac keeps quick targeted checks and
  anything macOS-only. ONE RUN PER SPRITE, EVERY STEP BOUNDED: `run`
  answers the command's status, or 76 (busy), 70 (the compiler does not
  build), 124/125 (a bound; `--for <minutes>` raises the command's), 137
  (out of memory), 75 (the Sprite did not answer), 74 (the provider did
  not answer) — and a failure's last line begins with the one of three
  that failed: SPRITE, CONNECTION or COMMAND. A RUN BELONGS TO THE
  SPRITE, NOT TO THE CONNECTION: a supervisor there keeps its output and
  status and holds the Sprite awake while it lives, `run` only follows
  it, and a dropped connection is followed again from the byte it stood
  at — so Ctrl-C or `work stop` ends a run; a drop, a hangup or the
  client being killed never does (it says so, and the next `run` answers
  76 until `work attach` has followed it out); a run is as long as its
  `--for` says, and the Sprite ends it at its bound whoever is
  watching (`work attach` follows again, `work stop` ends it, `work
  done` ends it with the lane). `sh tools/work sprites` shows all of
  them in seconds.
  A RUN ANSWERS ABOUT THIS WORKTREE OR NOT AT ALL: rsync carries files
  to the Sprite, a file the worktree no longer has is removed there by
  name, and the Sprite's manifest (every path and its hash) must equal
  the worktree's before anything starts — else `SPRITE — sync:` and 75.
  What a run wrote is left: `build/`, `.avra-cache`, anything git ignores.
  WHAT ENDS A RUN EARLY IS MEMORY, NOT TIME: a twenty-minute exec holds,
  chatty or silent, and thirty-two spinning processes leave a Sprite
  answering in a second — but a Sprite says 16 GB and a balloon holds
  half, more while it idles (3.3 to 7.3 GB were free to a run), there is
  no swap, and under about 250 MB the whole machine answers nobody for
  minutes. The Sprite's keeper ends a run at 600 MB (137), and every run
  says what it had to start with. A SPRITE WITH NO SESSION AND NO HOLD
  IS SUSPENDED WITHIN SECONDS, MID-WRITE IF NEED BE, which is why
  nothing runs there detached without the hold; one silent for minutes
  has lost its filesystem and is destroyed and created again
  (provisioning is `run`'s first step, from `.github/ci/packages.txt`).
  WHAT HOLDS A SPRITE AWAKE WITH NOBODY ATTACHED IS ITS TASKS API AND
  NOTHING ELSE WE TRIED, measured over 400 s without contact: a task
  refreshed each minute, no gap; a detached TTY session that prints, no
  gap; a running service, a 372 s gap; outbound traffic, frozen at once;
  an exec from outside every 20 s, one tick each. And a task's name is
  lowercase letters, digits and dashes or the Sprite answers 400 — a
  run is named after the machine that began it, capitals and all, so the
  hold is asked under a name made to fit and ITS ANSWER IS READ. A run
  that stood still says for how long in its own output, and `work
  sprites` shows it beside how long the run has been quiet.
- A BRANCH IS REBASED ONTO `origin/main` ONLY, never onto another
  unlanded branch: that lands the other branch's work unverified. A
  branch built on a stale local main moves with `git rebase --onto
  origin/main main <branch>`, which carries only its own commits.
- A PID IS CHECKED BEFORE IT IS KILLED. A recorded pid is reused once
  its process exits; read `ps -o command= -p <pid>` first.
- A TOOL IS RUN FOR REAL ONCE BEFORE IT BECOMES A DEFAULT. Fixtures
  prove the logic; a live run proves the path (a 62 MB upload hit a
  30 s client timeout that no fixture could reach).
- A GATE FLOOR IS RELATIVE (N − k), NEVER AN ABSOLUTE COUNT: the total
  moves when a branch deletes files, and an absolute floor then fails
  correct work.
- A CHANGE THE COMPILER CHECKS ABOUT ITS OWN SOURCE (a renamed type, a
  new license form) lands as a BRIDGE first: main's compiler must build
  the branch, because the seed and the gate's own build both use it.

## Working discipline

- NOTHING WE RUN TAKES MORE THAN A COUPLE OF MINUTES. Every command,
  build, wait and poll is bounded to ~2 minutes; the ONE exception is a
  full test run, which is ~5 minutes and runs on a Sprite. No `sleep`
  chains, no 10–60 minute timeouts, no loop that polls `main` or a build
  to infer progress. Break work into bounded steps: kick a long job off
  as ONE bounded background command, do useful work, then check ONCE. A
  `work wait` for a landing is bounded to a couple of minutes per call,
  never an hour, and it reads the PR's state, never `main`.
  A lane that blocks for minutes waiting is a defect in the lane, not
  patience. (Owner rule, 2026-10-02: an 18-minute `sleep` loop waiting on
  `main` deadlocked the merge queue — main could not move because that
  lane's own PR was failing the train.)

- GITHUB'S RUNNERS ARE THE ONLY GATE. `tools/gate_changed.sh` is the
  gate's checks in one definition — the static keepers, `fmt --check`
  on the changed `.av`, `check --baseline` on every affected package —
  and checks.yml runs it on every PR, plus the compiler-dependent
  keepers, the seed check and the affected packages' suites.
  `tools/work land`
  checks formatting alone, with the compiler the worktree already
  holds, and asks no other machine; a lane that wants the whole gate
  before pushing runs that script through `work run`.
- A GREEN PR LANDS ITSELF, AND A STALE ONE IS REFRESHED. An armed PR
  that falls behind `main` is updated by the watcher
  (`tools/pr_watcher.py`, `gh pr update-branch`) so "up to date" is met
  without a human; the watcher also arms a green PR, names a conflict
  and cancels a closed PR's run. `work status` shows each PR's check,
  its merge state and whether auto-merge is armed.
- MEASURE, THEN CHANGE. `make census CMD="check <pkg>"` gives EXACT
  retain/release/list-write counts and, with the per-caller tables,
  who causes them; `AVRA_SAMPLE=<secs> sh tools/watch.sh 6000 ./avra
  …` samples. Trust the census over the sample — and read
  `sample`'s output with its tree characters (`+ ! : |`) in mind,
  since parsing it as plain indentation reports the wrong fn.

- A TOOL IS RUN FOR REAL ONCE BEFORE IT BECOMES A DEFAULT. Fixtures
  prove the logic; a live run proves the path (a 62 MB upload hit a
  30 s client timeout that no fixture could reach).
- A GATE FLOOR IS RELATIVE (N − k), NEVER AN ABSOLUTE COUNT: the total
  moves when a branch deletes files, and an absolute floor then fails
  correct work.
- A CHANGE THE COMPILER CHECKS ABOUT ITS OWN SOURCE (a renamed type, a
  new license form) lands as a BRIDGE first: main's compiler must build
  the branch, because the seed and the gate's own build both use it.

## Working discipline

- NOTHING WE RUN TAKES MORE THAN A COUPLE OF MINUTES. Every command,
  build, wait and poll is bounded to ~2 minutes; the ONE exception is a
  full test run, which is ~5 minutes and runs on a Sprite. No `sleep`
  chains, no 10–60 minute timeouts, no loop that polls `main` or a build
  to infer progress. Break work into bounded steps: kick a long job off
  as ONE bounded background command, do useful work, then check ONCE. A
  `work wait` for a landing is bounded to a couple of minutes per call,
  never an hour, and it reads the PR's state, never `main`.
  A lane that blocks for minutes waiting is a defect in the lane, not
  patience. (Owner rule, 2026-10-02: an 18-minute `sleep` loop waiting on
  `main` deadlocked the merge queue — main could not move because that
  lane's own PR was failing the train.)

- GITHUB'S RUNNERS ARE THE ONLY GATE. `tools/gate_changed.sh` is the
  gate's checks in one definition — the static keepers, `fmt --check`
  on the changed `.av`, `check --baseline` on every affected package —
  and checks.yml runs it on every PR, plus the compiler-dependent
  keepers, the seed check and the affected packages' suites.
  `tools/work land`
  checks formatting alone, with the compiler the worktree already
  holds, and asks no other machine; a lane that wants the whole gate
  before pushing runs that script through `work run`.
- A GREEN PR LANDS ITSELF, AND A STALE ONE IS REFRESHED. An armed PR
  that falls behind `main` is updated by the watcher
  (`tools/pr_watcher.py`, `gh pr update-branch`) so "up to date" is met
  without a human; the watcher also arms a green PR, names a conflict
  and cancels a closed PR's run. `work status` shows each PR's check,
  its merge state and whether auto-merge is armed.
- MEASURE, THEN CHANGE. `make census CMD="check <pkg>"` gives EXACT
  retain/release/list-write counts and, with the per-caller tables,
  who causes them; `AVRA_SAMPLE=<secs> sh tools/watch.sh 6000 ./avra
  …` samples. Trust the census over the sample — and read
  `sample`'s output with its tree characters (`+ ! : |`) in mind,
  since parsing it as plain indentation reports the wrong fn.

#!/bin/sh
# THE PRE-GATE, on worktree /work/gate-wt of /work/avra. Two steps:
#   sh /work/gate.sh merge <base> [ref|file.bundle:branch]...
#       checks out <base> (a ref, or file.bundle:branch), merges the rest in order;
#       a conflict lists its files and stops (the tree is left mid-merge for a decision).
#   sh /work/gate.sh check [--rc FILE]... [--test FILE]...
#       the full gate on the worktree's HEAD, one heavy job at a time, every build cold,
#       every check as non-root user `gate`; GATE_SEED=<compiler> overrides the standing $src/build/avra. --rc runs AVRA_RC_GUARD=1 over a lone program
#       file (evaluator, native old path, native program layer; output vs its .expected);
#       --test runs `avra test FILE`. Each --rc case is also wrapped as a package for its
#       program-layer row, after a positive control that must abort under the guard. Every tools/witness_program_*.sh is run.
# Prints one table (check | result | detail | wall). Logs in /work/gate-logs/<run>/.
set -u
src=/work/avra
wt=/work/gate-wt
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB=12000

resolve() { # a ref, or file.bundle:branch fetched into refs/gate/<file>/<branch>
    case $1 in
        *.bundle:*)
            f=${1%%:*}; b=${1#*:}; [ -f "$f" ] || f=/work/$f
            n=$(basename "$f" .bundle)
            git -C "$src" fetch -q "$f" "+refs/heads/*:refs/gate/$n/*" || return 1
            echo "refs/gate/$n/$b" ;;
        *) echo "$1" ;;
    esac
}

if [ "${1:-}" = merge ]; then
    shift
    find "$src/.git" -name '._*' -delete 2>/dev/null
    [ -e "$wt/.git" ] || git -C "$src" worktree add -f --detach "$wt" program >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "gate: worktree add failed"; exit 2; }
    cd "$wt" || exit 2
    git merge --abort 2>/dev/null
    base=$(resolve "$1") || exit 3; shift
    git checkout -q -f --detach "$base" || { echo "gate: checkout $base failed"; exit 2; }
    git clean -q -f -d -e build/ >/dev/null
    echo "base $base = $(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD)"
    for m in "$@"; do
        r=$(resolve "$m") || exit 3
        if git -c user.name=gate -c user.email=gate@localhost merge -q --no-ff --no-edit "$r" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "merged $m ($(git rev-parse --short=8 "$r")) -> $(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD)"
        else
            echo "MERGE CONFLICT merging $m ($(git rev-parse --short=8 "$r")) onto $(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD):"
            git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | sed 's/^/  /'
            exit 4
        fi
    done
    exit 0

175692 /work/avra/CLAUDE.md
# Avra — clean-room compiler

## AVRA PRINCIPLES

The spec's Part 0 frames every decision (full text: spec, Part 0).
Above all: **P6, paradox collapse** — binary choices are usually false
dichotomies; find the design where both sides win. When a trade-off
feels forced, the model is wrong, not the requirements.

- P1  LLM-first: correct on first generation is the success metric
- P2  substrate for autonomous services
- P3  gloriously declarative, zero ceremony
- P4  Rust-level performance or better
- P5  full-stack vertical integration
- P6  paradox collapse
- P7  visible magic — always inspectable
- P8  escape hatches everywhere
- P9  boundaries are contracts
- P10 the compiler holds semantic knowledge no other tool has
- P11 machine-readability is the substrate, human-readability the projection
- P12 one source of truth, many projections
- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
- P17 composability over featurefulness

Clean restart of the Avra compiler, built slowly, one reviewed file at a
time. Front end first: an extensible grammar assembled from
LanguageFeature components, producing an AST for later passes.
Toolchain: the compiler builds itself — `./avra` runs `build/avra`,
and a cold tree bootstraps from `bootstrap/seed.ll.gz` (`make bootstrap`;
README.md).

Design sources of truth (in `../forge-crafting-intepreters`):
- `docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md` — the language
- `docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md` — node model, spans, error tolerance
- `bootstrap/docs/2026_08_19_STANDARDIZATION.md` — front-end shape

Follow the old tree's *documented designs*, never its code habits.

## Comments

Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.

## The idiom bar — BEFORE writing any fn

First drafts are written idiomatic, not cleaned up later. Before
the body exists, answer:

1. Is any loop a MAP/FILTER/FLAT-MAP? Comprehension (`?` works in
   element and iterable; predicates hoist into named fns).
2. Building head-plus-tail? `concat` (a list METHOD) / `flatten`
   (core's FREE fn — `flatten(xs)`, never `xs.flatten()`), never
   push-ceremony.
3. Is a projection being spelled twice? The second spelling names a
   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.
4. Does absence read straight? (`?? `, `?.`, if-null early return —
   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)
5. Scanning for one element? `find`/`any`/`index_of`, not a flag
   loop.
6. Unsure a shape compiles in the subset? PROBE in scratch first —
   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.

DOGFOODING.md is the full rulebook; `avra check --baseline
tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`
runs every package, `make idioms-accept` prunes what a fix made
gone). Every idiom the language can state is a `rule` declaration,
found by `avra check` itself, and the gate counts a RULE's finding
only — `type.alias_copy` wears the same `warning[kind]` shape and is
the compiler's own law, never a rule, so the gate reads the rule
table (`avra rules --json`), never a kind-string shape. Accepted
debt lives in the baseline alone, reviewed at adoption and every
time after. A new idiom lands in DOGFOODING's registry AT DISCOVERY,
named by its rule — `<module>.<rule>`, never a number.

## Style

- Inline single-use values. A `let` earns its place only when the
  name carries meaning the expression lacks, the value is read more
  than once, or the subset REQUIRES a pin (a `dyn` value selected
  among arms, a Result-answering lambda — "The subset today" names
  each). Empty literals (`[]`, `{}`) infer inline in
  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.
- A state struct's impl is its VOCABULARY: the small verbs that
  read or write its tables (`speak`, `bind`, `mint`, `give`) live
  as methods, so drivers read as prose. The free state fns the
  bootstrap habit left (`eval_node(ev, cx, e)`, the interpreter's
  `put(m, …)`, the backend's `define(em, …)`) are methods now, and
  so are the pass contexts' whole vocabularies (`cx.accepts(e,
  want)`, `cx.open_region(c)`, `ws.sig(d)` — 320 verbs, one sweep);
  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY
  POINT (`lower(a: Analysis)`, `memory(l: Lowered)`) keeps the one
  standard signature and is not a verb.
- A long fn splits at its PHASE boundaries into named helpers, each
  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —
  diagnostics/render.av). If a fn needs a paragraph comment
  mid-body, that paragraph is a helper's name.
- A LAW never assembles PROSE: every refusal is a NAMED VOICE fn
  (its whole body the one `spoken`/`emit`), in a voices section at
  the file's tail or shared where features share words. Rule
  bodies read as guard + verb (rule.compiler.refusal_assembled;
  enums/check.av is the exemplar).
  AND A VOICE STATES THE LAW, NOT THE SYMPTOM. "a pointer's only
  constant is null" is the rule; "both engines read it as null" was
  the observation that happened to hold the day it was written. A
  symptom-worded refusal goes STALE the moment the mechanism moves,
  and until then it reads as a workaround for a quirk rather than a
  rule to obey — so it teaches the reader to look for the quirk. The
  law's wording outlives its own implementation, which is what makes
  it worth pinning in the golden (lower.av's pointer-constant guard).
- A BUILDER'S WORDS ARE ITS CLAIM. A builder's refusal is carried
  WHOLE into its diagnostic (grammar/executor.av's build phase:
  `cause: Cause.Builder, message: m`), so a message that is a LAW
  the writer broke reads as the law, and one that is a DEFECT says

# Avra — clean-room compiler

## AVRA PRINCIPLES

The spec's Part 0 frames every decision (full text: spec, Part 0).
Above all: **P6, paradox collapse** — binary choices are usually false
dichotomies; find the design where both sides win. When a trade-off
feels forced, the model is wrong, not the requirements.

- P1  LLM-first: correct on first generation is the success metric
- P2  substrate for autonomous services
- P3  gloriously declarative, zero ceremony
- P4  Rust-level performance or better
- P5  full-stack vertical integration
- P6  paradox collapse
- P7  visible magic — always inspectable
- P8  escape hatches everywhere
- P9  boundaries are contracts
- P10 the compiler holds semantic knowledge no other tool has
- P11 machine-readability is the substrate, human-readability the projection
- P12 one source of truth, many projections
- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
- P17 composability over featurefulness

Clean restart of the Avra compiler, built slowly, one reviewed file at a
time. Front end first: an extensible grammar assembled from
LanguageFeature components, producing an AST for later passes.
Toolchain: the compiler builds itself — `./avra` runs `build/avra`,
and a cold tree bootstraps from `bootstrap/seed.ll.gz` (`make bootstrap`;
README.md).

Design sources of truth (in `../forge-crafting-intepreters`):
- `docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md` — the language
- `docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md` — node model, spans, error tolerance
- `bootstrap/docs/2026_08_19_STANDARDIZATION.md` — front-end shape

Follow the old tree's *documented designs*, never its code habits.

## Comments

Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.

## The idiom bar — BEFORE writing any fn

First drafts are written idiomatic, not cleaned up later. Before
the body exists, answer:

1. Is any loop a MAP/FILTER/FLAT-MAP? Comprehension (`?` works in
   element and iterable; predicates hoist into named fns).
2. Building head-plus-tail? `concat` (a list METHOD) / `flatten`
   (core's FREE fn — `flatten(xs)`, never `xs.flatten()`), never
   push-ceremony.
3. Is a projection being spelled twice? The second spelling names a
   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.
4. Does absence read straight? (`?? `, `?.`, if-null early return —
   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)
5. Scanning for one element? `find`/`any`/`index_of`, not a flag
   loop.
6. Unsure a shape compiles in the subset? PROBE in scratch first —
   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.

DOGFOODING.md is the full rulebook; `avra check --baseline
tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`
runs every package, `make idioms-accept` prunes what a fix made
gone). Every idiom the language can state is a `rule` declaration,
found by `avra check` itself, and the gate counts a RULE's finding
only — `type.alias_copy` wears the same `warning[kind]` shape and is
the compiler's own law, never a rule, so the gate reads the rule
table (`avra rules --json`), never a kind-string shape. Accepted
debt lives in the baseline alone, reviewed at adoption and every
time after. A new idiom lands in DOGFOODING's registry AT DISCOVERY,
named by its rule — `<module>.<rule>`, never a number.

## Style

- Inline single-use values. A `let` earns its place only when the
  name carries meaning the expression lacks, the value is read more
  than once, or the subset REQUIRES a pin (a `dyn` value selected
  among arms, a Result-answering lambda — "The subset today" names
  each). Empty literals (`[]`, `{}`) infer inline in
  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.
- A state struct's impl is its VOCABULARY: the small verbs that
  read or write its tables (`speak`, `bind`, `mint`, `give`) live
  as methods, so drivers read as prose. The free state fns the
  bootstrap habit left (`eval_node(ev, cx, e)`, the interpreter's
  `put(m, …)`, the backend's `define(em, …)`) are methods now, and
  so are the pass contexts' whole vocabularies (`cx.accepts(e,
  want)`, `cx.open_region(c)`, `ws.sig(d)` — 320 verbs, one sweep);
  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY
  POINT (`lower(a: Analysis)`, `memory(l: Lowered)`) keeps the one
  standard signature and is not a verb.
- A long fn splits at its PHASE boundaries into named helpers, each
  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —
  diagnostics/render.av). If a fn needs a paragraph

## Comments

Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.

## The idiom bar — BEFORE writing any fn

First drafts are written idiomatic, not cleaned up later. Before
the body exists, answer:

1. Is any loop a MAP/FILTER/FLAT-MAP? Comprehension (`?` works in
   element and iterable; predicates hoist into named fns).
2. Building head-plus-tail? `concat` (a list METHOD) / `flatten`
   (core's FREE fn — `flatten(xs)`, never `xs.flatten()`), never
   push-ceremony.
3. Is a projection being spelled twice? The second spelling names a
   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.
4. Does absence read straight? (`?? `, `?.`, if-null early return —
   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)
5. Scanning for one element? `find`/`any`/`index_of`, not a flag
   loop.
6. Unsure a shape compiles in the subset? PROBE in scratch first —
   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.
